docs.title: M22: Publish GitHub Release for v0.2.0 & Guard Duplicate PyPI Workflow Trigger
docs.text:
• Task ID: M22
  • Priority: P1 (Master Rank #11, Track B — Simple Fixes, Docs & CI Hygiene)
  • Status: Todo
  • Dependencies: M6, M11
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)
  • GitHub Project #5: Verity RedTeam Free Task Board

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
Tag v0.2.0 was published to PyPI, but the repository JMartynov/verityredteam-free has zero GitHub Releases — there is no structured, human-readable changelog entry for v0.2.0, no release assets, and no link from the GitHub UI to the shipped distribution.

Blocking issue: .github/workflows/workflow.yaml (lines 3–9) triggers the publish pipeline on both push: tags: ["v*"] and release: types: [published]:

on:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*"
  release:
    types: [published]
  workflow_dispatch:

Creating a GitHub Release for v0.2.0 therefore re-runs pypi-publish after the tag push already uploaded the artifacts, and pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish fails with 400 File already exists (duplicate filename for the same version). Without a guard, this task's core deliverable (the GitHub Release) is impossible to complete on a green CI run.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files
docs.text:
1. Guard .github/workflows/workflow.yaml against duplicate PyPI upload, using exactly one of:
  2. remove the release: types: [published] trigger so only tag pushes publish, or
  3. keep both triggers and add skip-existing: true to the pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1 step. The chosen guard must be explicit and verifiable by parsing the YAML (no comments-only guard).
  4. Add tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py that loads .github/workflows/workflow.yaml with yaml.safe_load and asserts:
  5. the effective trigger set is a subset of {push, release, workflow_dispatch}, and push.tags (if present) covers v*;
  6. a duplicate-upload guard exists: either release absent from on, or the publish step carries with.skip-existing: true;
  7. pypi-publish declares needs: full-tests, environment.name == pypi, and permissions.id-token: write.
  8. Publish the v0.2.0 GitHub Release with structured notes covering the M7–M11 deliverables, verified against the actual repository state, including an INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi container E2E confirmation.
  9. No regression to the existing release flow: a push of a new tag must still build, lint, test, and publish exactly once.

docs.title: 3. Automated Tests to Verify (tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py)
docs.text:
1. workflow.yaml parses cleanly with yaml.safe_load and exposes an on mapping (or list) with only known trigger keys.
  2. push.tags (when push is present) contains a pattern matching v* (e.g. "v*").
  3. Duplicate-upload guard assertion:
  4. release not in triggers → pass, or
  5. release in triggers and the pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish step has with: {skip-existing: true} → pass.
  6. any other combination → fail with an explicit message naming both remedies.
  7. pypi-publish job contract: needs == "full-tests", environment.name == "pypi", permissions["id-token"] == "write".
  8. Parametrized negative test: a mutated in-memory copy with release present and no skip-existing is rejected by the guard helper (pure-function check, no file writes).
  9. gh release view v0.2.0 --json tagName,body output contains the M7–M11 sections, the PyPI URL for verity-redteam-core==0.2.0, and the INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi E2E line (asserted via recorded fixture captured after publishing, not live network).

docs.title: 4. Acceptance Scenario in Clean Container with INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi
docs.text:
1. Apply the workflow guard, then run uv run pytest tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py -v locally — green.
  2. Push the guard commit and create the release: 
    gh release create v0.2.0 --title "v0.2.0" --notes-file docs/releases/v0.2.0.md
    (or --notes "…" with the same content) with sections for M7, M8, M9, M10, M11.
  3. Confirm the release exists and the notes are intact: 
    gh release view v0.2.0
  4. Confirm the test matrix stays green: the release event run of workflow.yaml must reach pypi-publish and either skip the already-present files (skip-existing) or not run at all because the release trigger was removed — no 400 File already exists failure.
  5. Container E2E against the PyPI artifact: 
    INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh
  6. Assertions: gh release view v0.2.0 exits 0 and shows tag v0.2.0; the release-triggered run does not fail on duplicate upload; INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh passes and installs verity-redteam-core==0.2.0 from PyPI.

docs.title: 5. Verification Commands
docs.text:
cd /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free
uv run ruff check src tests
uv run pytest tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py -v
uv run pytest tests/
gh release view v0.2.0
INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh

docs.title: 6. Acceptance Criteria
docs.text:
• [ ] .github/workflows/workflow.yaml has an explicit duplicate-upload guard (either the release: types: [published] trigger is removed, or pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish sets skip-existing: true).
  • [ ] tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py validates the workflow triggers and guard, including the parametrized negative case, and passes.
  • [ ] GitHub Release v0.2.0 is published on JMartynov/verityredteam-free with structured notes covering M7–M11 and a PyPI install link, verified by gh release view v0.2.0.
  • [ ] Re-triggering pypi-publish for an existing v0.2.0 no longer fails with a duplicate-filename error.
  • [ ] uv run pytest tests/, uv run ruff check src tests, and INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh pass cleanly.

docs.title: M23: Remove Stale "If the package is not yet on PyPI…" Caveat from README.md
docs.text:
• Task ID: M23
  • Priority: P1 (Master Rank #12, Track B — Simple Fixes, Docs & CI Hygiene)
  • Status: Todo
  • Dependencies: M10, M11
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)
  • GitHub Project #5: Verity RedTeam Free Task Board

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
README.md still contains a stale caveat above the quickstart:

If the package is not yet on PyPI, install from source or from a built wheel:

verity-redteam-core==0.2.0 is live on PyPI and installable via pip install verity-redteam-core and uvx --from verity-redteam-core. The caveat (a) contradicts the immediately preceding block that already shows the PyPI install, (b) undermines trust that the published package is authoritative, and (c) pushes contributor source-build steps onto end-user onboarding. tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py has no guard against this regression.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files

docs.title: M24: Extend Container E2E (verify_all_scenarios.sh) for DSN Credentials, CUSTOM_FIELD=sk-… & Live DVMCP stdio Probing
docs.text:
• Task ID: M24
  • Priority: P2 (Master Rank #13, Track B — Simple Fixes, Docs & CI Hygiene)
  • Status: Todo
  • Dependencies: M8, M11
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
MultiClientConfigScanner (src/verity/discovery/config_scanner.py) separates key-name matching (SECRET_KEY_PATTERNS) from value-shape matching (SECRET_VALUE_PATTERNS). M11 added DSN credential detection (DATABASE_URL / postgres://user:pass@host/db-style values) and M7/M11 extended value-shape coverage, but the container E2E suite never exercises either behaviour:

  • Scenario 1 configs contain only sk-, ghp_ and placeholder env values; no DSN with an embedded password and no secret under an arbitrary (non-secret-looking) key name such as CUSTOM_FIELD.
  • SECRETS=( … ) in tests/e2e_containers/verify_all_scenarios.sh has no DSN password or arbitrary-key secret, so a redaction regression in _scrub_secrets() (src/verity/cli.py) could leak raw values into terminal / json / markdown / html output undetected.
  • DVMCP coverage is static-only: Scenario 4 runs verity scan --path /opt/dvmcp. The live probe path (verity test --command "python3 …") is only exercised against the synthetic vuln_stdio_mcp.py fixture, so a real DVMCP challenge server is never handshaked against, listed, or probed over stdio.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files
docs.text:
1. DSN credential coverage: extend the generated ~/.cursor/mcp.json in Scenario 1 with a server whose env carries DATABASE_URL: postgres://analytics:<password>@db.internal:5432/analytics (embedded password) plus a CUSTOM_FIELD holding a sk-… literal (arbitrary key name, value-pattern-only detection).
  2. Safe twin: add a second server using DATABASE_URL: postgres://analytics:${DB_PASS}@db.internal:5432/analytics; it must produce zero secret findings (no detection, no masking artefacts).
  3. Leak assertions: append the raw DSN password and the sk-… literal to the SECRETS=( … ) array so both scan_for_leaks passes (pre-snapshot and post-snapshot) cover them.
  4. Live DVMCP probing: in addition to the existing static verity scan --path /opt/dvmcp, add a live stdio probe verity test --command "python3 /opt/dvmcp/<challenge_script>.py" (both terminal and --format json), asserting exit 1 and at least one FAIL result carrying VERITY-STATIC-* rule ids.
  5. Parity: the same DSN shapes accepted by MultiClientConfigScanner must be redacted by _scrub_secrets() in all four report formats — no drift between detection and masking.

1. DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:SuperSecretDbPassword123@db:5432/app → flagged SEC-STATIC-SECRET-IN-CONFIG; raw password absent from terminal / json / markdown / html output (parametrized over the four formats); matched value rendered as ****.
  2. DATABASE_URL=postgres://app:${DB_PASS}@db:5432/app and $DB_PASS-style references → not flagged.
  3. CUSTOM_FIELD=sk-live-… (non-secret key name) → flagged via value pattern; scrubbed to ****.
  4. mysql://user:pass@host/db and mongodb+srv://user:pass@cluster/db DSN variants → flagged and scrubbed.
  5. Benign values (DATABASE_URL=postgres://app@db:5432/app, REDIS_URL=redis://cache:6379/0, DB_POOL_SIZE=10) → zero findings.
  6. Parity test: every DSN shape detected by MultiClientConfigScanner.is_secret_env_entry() is redacted to **** by the CLI scrubber in each report format (no detection/masking drift).

docs.title: M25: Add Nightly schedule Trigger (cron: '0 4 * * *') to e2e-containers.yml
docs.text:
• Task ID: M25
  • Priority: P2 (Master Rank #14, Track B — Simple Fixes, Docs & CI Hygiene)
  • Status: Todo

  • GitHub Project #5: Verity RedTeam Free Task Board

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
.github/workflows/e2e-containers.yml currently runs only on workflow_dispatch, version tag pushes (v*), and pull requests touching src/**, README.md, or tests/e2e_containers/**. It has no scheduled execution.

The container E2E suite installs upstream artifacts at runtime: - PyPI packages resolved by uv sync --extra dev / wheel installation. - mcp-remote@0.1.15 via npx. - DVMCP. - Docker base images.

Without a nightly run, upstream drift or yanked package versions can break the ground-zero install path between releases. .github/workflows/full-tests.yml already has a nightly schedule at cron: '0 3 * * *'; e2e-containers.yml should run at cron: '0 4 * * *' so the heavier container suite executes after the full test suite and still every night.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files
docs.text:
1. Workflow Trigger: Add to .github/workflows/e2e-containers.yml: 
    schedule:
  - cron: '0 4 * * *'
  2. Preserve Existing Triggers: Keep workflow_dispatch, push: tags: - "v*", and the existing pull_request path filters unchanged.
  3. Offset From Full Tests: Use 0 4 * * * (one hour after full-tests.yml at 0 3 * * *) to avoid runner contention and catch daily upstream drift in PyPI packages, mcp-remote@0.1.15, DVMCP, and Docker base images.
  4. Workflow Hygiene Test: Add tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py coverage that loads .github/workflows/e2e-containers.yml with yaml.safe_load and asserts the 0 4 * * * schedule exists alongside workflow_dispatch, tag pushes, and pull_request.
  5. Container E2E Acceptance Run: The scheduled job must continue to run bash ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh with INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel.

  2. test_e2e_containers_preserves_existing_triggers: assert workflow_dispatch, push.tags == ["v*"], and pull_request.paths are present.
  3. test_schedule_offset_differs_from_full_tests: parse both workflows and assert e2e-containers.yml uses 0 4 * * * while full-tests.yml uses 0 3 * * *.
  4. test_e2e_containers_runs_container_suite: assert the workflow still invokes bash ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh with INSTALL_SOURCE: wheel.

1. Open a pull request containing the workflow change and confirm e2e-containers still runs through its existing pull_request trigger.
  2. Use workflow_dispatch to confirm manual execution remains available.
  3. Confirm GitHub Actions registers the workflow with a nightly schedule entry at 0 4 * * *.
  4. Wait for or simulate the scheduled run and confirm INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel bash ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh completes successfully.
  5. Assertions: the YAML parse test passes; workflow_dispatch, tag v*, and pull_request triggers remain intact; the scheduled container verification runs nightly and fails loudly on upstream drift.

docs.title: M26: Upgrade actions/checkout and astral-sh/setup-uv Pins Across All GitHub Actions Workflows
docs.text:
• Task ID: M26
  • Priority: P3 (Master Rank #15, Track B — Simple Fixes, Docs & CI Hygiene)
  • Status: Todo
  • Dependencies: M6, M8
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)
  • GitHub Project #5: Verity RedTeam Free Task Board

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
All four GitHub Actions workflows pin third-party actions to versions that still run on the Node 20 runtime, which GitHub has deprecated and now annotates on every run:

  • .github/workflows/ci.yml — actions/checkout@v4, astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
  • .github/workflows/full-tests.yml — actions/checkout@v4, astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
  • .github/workflows/workflow.yaml — actions/checkout@v4, astral-sh/setup-uv@v4
  • .github/workflows/e2e-containers.yml — actions/checkout@v4, astral-sh/setup-uv@v5

Result: every CI run emits Node.js 20 actions are deprecated warnings, the setup-uv pin is inconsistent across workflows (v4 vs v5), and workflow.yaml gates the PyPI publish so its warnings pollute release runs. A hard runtime cut-over to Node 24 will break the v4 pins outright.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files
docs.text:
1. actions/checkout: bump v4 → v5 (Node 24 runtime) in all four workflows.
  2. astral-sh/setup-uv: bump to v6 (Node 24 runtime) in all four workflows — including .github/workflows/e2e-containers.yml, which is currently v5 — so a single pin is used everywhere.
  3. No legacy pins: zero occurrences of actions/checkout@v4 and zero occurrences of astral-sh/setup-uv@v4 / astral-sh/setup-uv@v5 in .github/workflows/**.
  4. No floating refs: no @main / @master action references introduced by the migration.
  5. No behavioural change: job names, triggers, matrices, env blocks, permissions, and step ordering stay identical; only uses: version tags change.

Target files: - .github/workflows/ci.yml - .github/workflows/full-tests.yml - .github/workflows/workflow.yaml - .github/workflows/e2e-containers.yml - tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py (new)

docs.title: 3. Automated Tests to Verify (tests/unit/test_workflow_hygiene.py)
docs.text:
1. Parametrized over all four workflow files: every uses: actions/checkout@… equals actions/checkout@v5.
  2. Parametrized over all four workflow files: every uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@… equals astral-sh/setup-uv@v6.
  3. setup-uv@v4 and checkout@v4 appear zero times across .github/workflows/** (directory-wide grep-style scan).
  4. No action reference uses a floating @main / @master branch.
  5. Pin parity: the set of actions/checkout@… tags across the four workflows has size 1, and likewise for astral-sh/setup-uv@… (prevents future drift).
  6. Workflow YAML still parses and every expected job name (test-and-build, full-tests, pypi-publish, e2e-containers) is present.

  2. CI job assertions: the CI workflow completes green on Python 3.12 and 3.13 with zero Node.js 20 actions are deprecated annotations on the run summary.
  3. Full suite assertions: Full Test Suite runs green on 3.12 / 3.13; Verify Zero-Docker Demo Targets CLI, Verify SQL AST Guard CLI and Verify MCP Server CLI steps still pass unchanged.
  4. Release path: Publish to PyPI workflow reaches the full-tests job and builds uv build artefacts without deprecation warnings.
  5. Container E2E: INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh passes (e2e-containers.yml bumped to the same pins).
  6. Confirm no remaining @v4 action pins in the workflow directory after the change.

docs.title: M27: Guard uv build & Local Wheel Staging in run_e2e.sh When INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi
docs.text:
• Task ID: M27
  • Priority: P3 (Master Rank #16, Track B — Simple Fixes, Docs & CI Hygiene)
  • Status: Todo
  • Dependencies: M8, M11
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)
  • GitHub Project #5: Verity RedTeam Free Task Board

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh (lines 21–36) unconditionally runs uv build and stages the freshly built wheel into the local staging directory (.wheel_stage/) before invoking Docker Compose, regardless of INSTALL_SOURCE.

When INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi: - The wheel build is never consumed by any customer container (they install from PyPI), so build time is wasted on every run. - Staging still copies a wheel, and stale *.whl files left in dist/ can be selected and staged — or picked up later when the same checkout is rerun in wheel mode — leading to tests exercising an outdated artifact.

The build and staging steps must be guarded behind if [ "$INSTALL_SOURCE" = "wheel" ]; then … fi, while still ensuring the staging directory exists so the Docker build context never fails.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files
docs.text:
1. Guard build + staging in tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh (lines 21–36): 
    if [ "$INSTALL_SOURCE" = "wheel" ]; then
  …
fi
    uv build, wheel discovery, and wheel copy into .wheel_stage/ must run only in wheel mode.
  2. Directory invariant: .wheel_stage/ (or the configured staging dir) must always exist (mkdir -p) regardless of INSTALL_SOURCE, so the Docker build context and Dockerfile COPY never fail in pypi mode.
  3. Stale artifact hygiene: before building, remove previous wheel(s) from both dist/ and the staging directory (e.g. rm -f dist/verity_redteam_core-*.whl and clearing staged wheels) to guarantee a fresh artifact is used.
  4. Fail-fast preserved: in wheel mode, if uv build produces no verity_redteam_core-*.whl, exit non-zero with a clear message. In pypi mode, no wheel check is performed and the run proceeds.
  5. Compose wiring unchanged: docker compose build --build-arg INSTALL_SOURCE="$INSTALL_SOURCE" continues to receive the selected mode in both branches.
  6. Testability: build/staging logic must be observable from a shell/unit test in tests/unit/test_e2e_runner_hygiene.py (e.g. static assertions on the script plus an executable harness that stubs uv and docker compose).

docs.title: 3. Automated Tests to Verify (tests/unit/test_e2e_runner_hygiene.py)
docs.text:
1. INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi: uv build is not invoked, no wheel is copied into .wheel_stage/, and docker compose build still receives INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi (parametrized with default/unset value resolving to wheel or documented default).
  2. INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel: stale dist/verity_redteam_core-*.whl and staged wheels are removed before uv build; fresh wheel is discovered and copied into .wheel_stage/.
  3. Staging directory (.wheel_stage/) exists after the script's setup phase in both modes.
  4. INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel with a stubbed uv build producing no wheel → script exits non-zero with the expected message; INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi under the same stub → script does not fail on missing wheel.
  5. Script hygiene: bash -n tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh and (if available) shellcheck pass.

docs.text:
Run the container E2E suite in both install modes from a clean checkout:

  1. Wheel mode 
    INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh
  2. uv build runs, stale wheels are cleared first, .wheel_stage/ contains exactly the freshly built verity_redteam_core-*.whl.

  3. All customer containers (customer-pip, customer-uvx, customer-full-workstation) pass.

  4. PyPI mode 

    INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh

  5. uv build is not invoked and no local wheel is staged; .wheel_stage/ still exists so the Docker build context is valid.

  6. All customer containers install from PyPI and pass.

  7. Stale-wheel regression

  8. Seed dist/ with an older verity_redteam_core-0.0.0-*.whl, then run INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh.
  9. Assertions: the stale artifact is removed before build, no log/line references the seeded stale version, and the run passes using only the newly built wheel.

uv run pytest tests/unit/test_e2e_runner_hygiene.py -v

INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh
INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi ./tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh

• [ ] uv build and wheel staging in tests/e2e_containers/run_e2e.sh run only when INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel.
  • [ ] .wheel_stage/ always exists before docker compose build, regardless of INSTALL_SOURCE.
  • [ ] Stale wheels in dist/ and the staging directory are removed before building; a seeded stale wheel is never used.
  • [ ] Missing wheel in wheel mode fails fast; pypi mode proceeds without any build or wheel check.

docs.title: M28: Fix Retired verity-core Package Name in AGENTS.md & Extend Documentation Parity Guard
docs.text:
• Task ID: M28
  • Priority: P3 (Master Rank #17, Track B — Simple Fixes, Docs & CI Hygiene)
  • Status: Todo
  • Dependencies: M10
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)
  • GitHub Project #5: Verity RedTeam Free Task Board

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
AGENTS.md still identifies the repository by its retired distribution name verity-core on line 5 (project identity block) and again in the plugin/MCP section, even though the package now ships as verity-redteam-core. The same block also hardcodes the stale task range "Tasks M1–M6", which no longer reflects the live board.

tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py::test_no_stale_package_references guards against this drift, but its _STALE_PACKAGE_RE scan iterates only over README.md and docs/extensibility.md. AGENTS.md is never validated, so the retired name survives every CI run.

Result: agent-facing documentation contradicts pyproject.toml and the README, and the parity guard does not cover the one file agents read first.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files
docs.text:
1. Rename in AGENTS.md: replace every verity-core occurrence with verity-redteam-core in the Project Identity header (line 5) and the open-core plugin boundary section (line 12), keeping the parenthetical repo path unchanged.
  2. Task board reference: replace the hardcoded "Tasks M1–M6" range with a non-stale pointer to TASK_BOARD.md / GitHub Project #5.
  3. Extend the parity guard: in tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py, extend test_no_stale_package_references to include REPO_ROOT / "AGENTS.md", and introduce an AGENTS_PATH constant alongside README_PATH and EXTENSIBILITY_PATH so future docs are added in one place.
  4. Optional hardening: teach _extract_verity_commands() to also parse YAML (yaml) fenced blocks in README.md, validating the verity scan/verity test command lines inside the GitHub Actions CI snippet, not only shell fences.
  5. Zero behavioural change: no src/ edits; documentation and test guard only.

docs.title: 1. Context & Problem Statement
docs.text:
The Task Matrix in TASK_BOARD.md links rows M1–M11 only to the generic Project #5 root URL (https://github.com/users/JMartynov/projects/5), while rows M12–M29 carry the exact item id ([View Item #M12](https://github.com/users/JMartynov/projects/5) (\PVTI_…`)). The same gap exists in the detailed### M:sections: their#### Task Specblocks forM1–M10omit theGitHub Project #5 Item: `PVTI_…`identifier thatM11–M29` use.

Consequences:

  • A reader cannot navigate from a board row to the concrete project item; the link always lands on Project #5 view 1.
  • Nothing prevents the same drift when new rows are added, because no test asserts the matrix/detailed-section/id relationship.
  • Manual reconciliation (search by title in the GitHub UI) is required after every board edit.

docs.title: 2. Requirements & Target Files
docs.text:
1. Harvest canonical item ids (execution time, never guessed). Run gh project item-list 5 --owner JMartynov --format json --limit 100 and persist the payload (e.g. /tmp/project5_items.json), then map each task row M<n> to its item by matching the task key/title prefix (e.g. M11:) in the item content title. Record the item id field verbatim (shape PVTI_…). Do not invent, reorder or truncate ids. If an existing row has no matching item, stop and report it instead of writing a placeholder.
  2. Matrix normalization in TASK_BOARD.md for M1–M11 and for any other matrix row missing an id: follow the exact convention already used by M12–M29 — [View Item #M<n>](https://github.com/users/JMartynov/projects/5) (\PVTI_…`)` — keeping the root URL and appending the id in backticks. Do not alter other columns, ordering or wording.
  3. Detailed-section normalization: for every ### M<n>: heading whose #### Task Spec / reference block lacks it, add GitHub Project #5 Item: \PVTI_…``. Preserve all existing spec text; the id must equal the matrix id for the same row.
  4. Scope guard. All added validation must discover rows dynamically from TASK_BOARD.md (regex such as ^\| \*\*M(\d+)\*\* \| and ^### M(\d+):) so the guarantees hold automatically across all rows M1–M29.
  5. Parity test in tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py (new or extended, no new dependencies) covering every discovered row:
  6. matrix row contains an id matching PVTI_[A-Za-z0-9_-]{10,};
  7. matrix row links to https://github.com/users/JMartynov/projects/5;
  8. the spec link resolves to an existing docs/tasks/*.md file, or is the documented Inline below marker with a matching ### M<n>: heading in the same file;
  9. the detailed section for that row exists and contains the same id;
  10. ids are unique across rows; the matrix row set equals the detailed heading set.
  11. No runtime/source changes, no new dependencies, no report-format changes.

docs.title: Python AST Real-World Rules & Import Aliases
Context & Objectives
docs.text:
The Python AST scanner must catch the same dangerous sinks in real MCP server code that it currently catches only in synthetic fixtures. Two gaps remain:

  1. Aliased imports (import pickle as p, from subprocess import Popen as run_cmd) bypass dotted-name dispatch because visit_Call never consults the alias map.
  2. Two rules (VERITY-AST-CWE-22-TRAVERSAL, VERITY-AST-CWE-862-BOLA) still depend on literal marker strings (is_traversal, is_cross_tenant) that never appear in customer code.

This task replaces marker-string heuristics with real AST def-use analysis, resolves import aliases before rule dispatch, and adds a genuine SQL-injection AST rule so findings on real-world MCP servers are deterministic and defensible.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
File Change src/verity/scanner/python_ast.py Alias-aware dispatch plus three real AST rules tests/unit/scanner/test_python_ast.py Paired vulnerable/benign controls per rule

Out of scope: non-Python languages, rules not listed below, and any change to existing RuleCatalog identifiers or severity assignments.

docs.title: M39.1 — Wire the import alias map into call dispatch
docs.text:
visit_Import and visit_ImportFrom already populate self.imports (python_ast.py#L63-L76), but visit_Call (#L133-L222) only inspects literal ast.Name / ast.Attribute chains. Resolve the leftmost name of an attribute chain through self.imports before rule dispatch so aliases map to canonical dotted names:

  • import pickle as p then p.loads(buf) resolves to pickle.loads.
  • from subprocess import Popen as run_cmd then run_cmd(cmd, shell=True) resolves to subprocess.Popen.
  • Attribute-chain rewriting must be safe: rewrite only the root name, leave intermediate attributes untouched, and never raise on unknown roots.

docs.title: M39.2 — Real CWE-22 traversal def-use check
docs.text:
Replace the synthetic is_traversal string check with a parameter-to-sink def-use analysis for VERITY-AST-CWE-22-TRAVERSAL. A finding requires all three conditions:

  1. A function parameter, or a value derived from one, reaches a path sink: builtin open, pathlib.Path, os.path.join, or os.open.
  2. The sink result is not contained by Path.resolve plus Path.is_relative_to, os.path.realpath, or os.path.commonpath.
  3. The tainted value is not a module-level Constant.

Benign construction such as open(os.path.join(BASE_DIR, "static", name)) combined with a containment check must not fire.

docs.title: M39.3 — Real CWE-89 SQL injection AST rule
docs.text:
Add a real AST rule for VERITY-AST-CWE-89-SQLI covering cursor.execute, cursor.executemany, connection.execute, session.raw, and session.text. Flag when the SQL argument is:

  • a JoinedStr (f-string) containing a non-constant expression,
  • a Call to .format(...) on a string literal, or
  • a BinOp using % where the left operand is a string literal and the right operand is parameter- or input-derived.

Parameterized calls whose SQL argument is a Constant string, with or without a separate params tuple, must not fire.

docs.title: M39.4 — Real CWE-862 BOLA AST rule
docs.text: Replace the synthetic bola_violation / is_cross_tenant strings with a real rule for VERITY-AST-CWE-862-BOLA: a function decorated with @mcp.tool (or an equivalent tool registration) that queries by a record identifier (get_*, fetch_*, find_*, read_* on a session, cursor, or repository object) whose body contains no tenant/session ownership check (session_tenant, current_user, owner_id, tenant_id comparison) and no authorization guard.

docs.title: Free CLI SARIF Pro Gate & Line Precision
Context & Objectives
docs.text:
--format sarif is a Verity Pro capability, but the Free CLI must describe that boundary honestly and deterministically. Two properties matter to a CI customer:

  1. A Free installation asked for SARIF never writes a partial or empty artifact; it returns the structured PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED error and exit code 2.
  2. When verity-pro is installed, the exported SARIF preserves the real source line and the real file path instead of collapsing every result to startLine: 1.

This task hardens the Free CLI gate and the line-number propagation only.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
File Change src/verity/cli.py Pro-plugin gate for --format sarif and real line/path propagation tests/unit/cli/test_sarif_pro_gate.py Gate and paired Pro-present control tests/unit/cli/test_sarif_line_precision.py Line propagation and startLine == 1 fallback

Out of scope: any reporting engine internals outside the Free CLI surface.

docs.title: Pro-only gate
docs.text:
• _pro_plugin_available() remains the single source of truth for edition detection.
  • When the verity-pro plugin is absent and --format sarif is requested, the CLI must emit the structured PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED payload and return exit code 2.
  • No output file is created or truncated when the gate fires, even if --output was supplied.
  • No unhandled traceback escapes; the failure is the structured error only.

docs.title: Line and path precision
docs.text:
When the plugin is present, every SARIF result must carry:

  • physicalLocation.artifactLocation.uri set to the real file_path from the finding.
  • physicalLocation.region.startLine set to finding.get('line_number') or finding.get('line') or 1.

A finding without a usable location must degrade to startLine == 1 rather than omitting the region or crashing.

docs.title: Free MCP Database Guard Pro Gating
Context & Objectives
docs.text:
The Free verity_database_guard tool serves SQL validation. Two of its actions belong to Verity Pro: NoSQL filter validation and response-volume enforcement. On a Free installation those actions must fail closed with a structured PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED error rather than importing Pro modules or approximating the check.

This task implements only the Free gating behaviour.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
File Change src/verity/mcp_server/handlers/database.py Edition gate for the two Pro-only actions tests/unit/mcp_server/test_database_guard_pro_gating.py Gate and benign Free-action tests

Out of scope: the Pro guard implementations themselves and any other MCP tool.

docs.title: Contract
docs.text:
When the verity-pro plugin is absent:

  • verity_database_guard(action="validate_nosql_filter", ...) returns {"error": "PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED", "feature": "validate_nosql_filter"}.
  • verity_database_guard(action="enforce_volume_policy", ...) returns {"error": "PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED", "feature": "enforce_volume_policy"}.
  • Neither path performs guard logic, and neither imports a Pro-only filter or volume guard module. The gate is evaluated before any import of optional dependencies.
  • The response is a normal tool result; the MCP server keeps serving later requests.

The Free validate_query action continues to work exactly as before, including on the same server instance that just returned a PRO_FEATURE_REQUIRED result.

docs.title: Context & Objectives
docs.text:
Two Free components carry fixture-coupled behaviour:

  1. The read-only guard misses several destructive verbs that real MCP servers expose (run_sql, execute_sql, upsert, post_, put_, patch_, chmod, kill).
  2. The dual-path router injects a hardcoded "formula": "1 + 1" argument for unknown tools, which fabricates caller intent instead of reflecting the target schema.

This task hardens the guard and removes the hardcoded payload from the router while preserving known-tool arguments verbatim.

Out of scope: transport probing and any Phase 2 mutation logic.

docs.text:

  • Read-only tools such as list_customers remain permitted.
  • Argument scanning behaviour is unchanged: destructive SQL and shell payloads are still blocked recursively, and phase != PHASE_1 still bypasses the guard.

docs.title: Dual-path router
docs.text:
• For unknown tools, the router must not inject the hardcoded "formula": "1 + 1".
  • Instead it emits the schema's required-argument skeleton with neutral type-correct values, or an explicit NEEDS_ARGS marker when a required argument cannot be synthesised safely.
  • Known-tool arguments are preserved verbatim; no synthesised value overwrites a caller-supplied argument.

docs.title: M7: CLI Parity, ConsolidatedSecurityAuditor Wiring & YAML Config Support
docs.text:
• Task ID: M7
  • Priority: P0
  • Status: Done
  • Dependencies: None (M1–M6 completed)
  • Blocks: M8, M9, M10
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)
  • GitHub Project #5: Verity RedTeam Free Task Board

docs.title: 1. Problem Statement & Context
docs.text:
A codebase-vs-documentation audit of verity-redteam-core revealed critical parity gaps between what the README/product promises for verity scan and what the CLI actually executes today:

  1. verity scan bypasses ConsolidatedSecurityAuditor:
  2. In src/verity/cli.py (_collect_config_findings, L155–L191; _cmd_scan, L281–L298), verity scan (both default 9-client discovery and --config-file) only calls MultiClientConfigScanner and passes {"name": config.server_name, **raw} to StaticRuleEvaluator.scan_tool().
  3. Meanwhile, ConsolidatedSecurityAuditor (src/verity/discovery/auditor.py, L27–L163) already implements:
    • Plaintext secret detection in config.env (SEC-STATIC-SECRET-IN-CONFIG, FindingSeverity.HIGH, redacted evidence KEY=****),
    • Unsafe shell execution wrapper detection (SEC-STATIC-UNSAFE-SHELL-WRAPPER, FindingSeverity.MEDIUM for sh/bash/zsh/cmd/powershell),
    • Hybrid tri-layer Passport fingerprinting (HybridDiscoveryMatcher / mcp-fingerprints), and
    • Offline OSV CVE correlation (VulnerabilityLookupEngine / mcp-vulnerabilities, e.g., catching mcp-remote@0.1.15 / CVE-2025-6514 as VULN-<id>).
  4. Because cli.py never invokes ConsolidatedSecurityAuditor, running verity scan on a workstation config with leaked env credentials, raw bash -c wrappers, or known-vulnerable pinned npm/PyPI MCP packages reports 0 findings unless a tool schema itself happens to match a static rule.
  5. YAML IDE configs silently fail:
  6. MultiClientConfigScanner.get_standard_client_paths() (src/verity/discovery/config_scanner.py, L153, L162–L163) registers .continue/config.yaml and librechat.yaml, yet parse_config_file() (config_scanner.py, L199–L204) and _collect_config_findings() (cli.py, L169–L177) only call json.loads(), silently returning [] or raising Invalid JSON on YAML configs.
  7. Stale CLI template in ActiveExploitBridge:
  8. src/verity/discovery/active_bridge.py (L44) defines DEFAULT_CLI_COMMAND_TEMPLATE = "verity test --server '{package}' --vuln '{vuln_id}'", referencing --server and --vuln flags that do not exist in src/verity/cli.py (L506–L519).
  9. SARIF plugin entry-point mismatch:
  10. _load_sarif_exporter() (src/verity/cli.py, L46–L54) looks only for entry points named "sarif" or "sarif_export" in group "verity.plugins", whereas ../verityredteam/pyproject.toml registers "pro" (verity_pro.plugin:register_pro_extensions).

Scope Decision (Confirmed): Fix these CLI parity bugs first (M7) before executing ground-zero empty-container verification (M8), demo GIF recording (M9), and customer README restructuring (M10), so every customer claim is 100% real and reproducible.

docs.title: 2.1 Wire ConsolidatedSecurityAuditor into verity scan
docs.text:
• Files: src/verity/cli.py (L155–L191, L233–L298, L488–L504), src/verity/discovery/auditor.py (L27–L175)
  • Requirements:
  • Update _collect_config_findings() (or add a clean helper called by _collect_scan_data()) to run ConsolidatedSecurityAuditor.audit_server(config, live_probe=...) on every discovered DiscoveredServerConfig in addition to StaticRuleEvaluator.scan_tool() schema checks.
  • Ensure verity scan continues to run fast (< 5s) and offline-safe by default (i.e., do not block or crash if network is unavailable or offline caches are empty; gracefully reuse cached/bundled data from mcp-fingerprints / mcp-vulnerabilities / data_fetcher.py). Optionally expose --live-probe / --offline flags if needed without breaking existing default verity scan behavior.
  • Strict Credential Scrubbing Guarantee: Plaintext secret values from config.env MUST NEVER appear unmasked in terminal, json, markdown, or html output — only redacted evidence (KEY=****) and rule SEC-STATIC-SECRET-IN-CONFIG.
  • Normalize SecurityAuditFinding records seamlessly into _normalize_finding() so Summary severity counts (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, INFO), --fail-on-findings exit code 1, --format {terminal,json,markdown,html}, and --output all work uniformly across config findings, static rule findings, OSV CVE findings, and --path AST findings.
  • Ensure verity scan --config-file <path> can match mcp-remote@0.1.15 (and similar versioned npm/PyPI server specs in command/args) against offline OSV advisories from mcp-vulnerabilities / data_fetcher.py.

docs.text:
• Task ID: M8

docs.title: 1. Problem Statement & Goal
docs.text: To make sure every customer workflow documented in README.md works reliably in the real world (not just against host-cached dev environments or editable workspace installs), we must validate verity-redteam-core inside empty, clean containers from scratch: - Zero pre-installed verity package, - Zero editable source mounts from the host repository, - Zero host ~/.cursor / ~/.claude / ~/.cache/verity mounts, - Fresh installation of verity-redteam-core, - Fresh installation of both real open-source vulnerable MCP servers and deterministic self-contained vulnerable fixtures, - Automated execution of all 6 customer scenarios, asserting exact exit codes, expected Rule IDs/CWEs, secret scrubbing, and valid report artifacts, while capturing sanitized verbatim CLI output snapshots for M10.

docs.title: 2. Confirmed Decisions & Architecture
docs.text:
1. Package Install Toggle (INSTALL_SOURCE):
  2. INSTALL_SOURCE=wheel (default right now before PyPI release): Builds a clean distribution wheel via uv build (dist/verity_redteam_core-*.whl), copies only the .whl file into the fresh container, and runs pip install /tmp/dist/*.whl (or uvx --from /tmp/dist/*.whl verity ...).
  3. INSTALL_SOURCE=pypi: Installs directly from live PyPI (pip install verity-redteam-core and uvx --from verity-redteam-core verity ...) once v0.1.0+ is published.
  4. Both Vulnerable Target Tiers Installed From Scratch:
  5. Tier A — Real Public Vulnerable MCP Packages:
    • Pinned mcp-remote@0.1.15 (npm package with known CVE-2025-6514 in mcp-vulnerabilities OSV database), installed inside the container to verify real config/OSV CVE detection.
    • Open-source DVMCP (Damn Vulnerable MCP Server, harishsg993010/damn-vulnerable-mcp-server, pinned commit/tag) installed inside the container and probed live + scanned via Python AST.
  6. Tier B — Deterministic Self-Contained Vulnerable Fixtures (tests/e2e_containers/fixtures/):
    • Standalone installable vulnerable Python MCP server fixture (stdio and HTTP/SSE modes) exposing poisoned tool descriptions (VERITY-STATIC-INJECTION-OVERRIDE CWE-74, VERITY-STATIC-TOOL-POISONING CWE-358, VERITY-STATIC-EXFIL-WEBHOOK CWE-200, VERITY-STATIC-METADATA-SSRF CWE-918) plus unsafe Python handler code (eval() CWE-94, subprocess.run(..., shell=True) CWE-78, yaml.load() CWE-502) for verity scan --path.
    • Realistic generated workstation IDE configs created clean inside the container's $HOME (~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json, ~/.continue/config.yaml, ./.mcp.json) containing plaintext API keys/DB URLs, a raw bash -c wrapper, and mcp-remote@0.1.15.
    • Adversarial SQL payload corpus (; DROP TABLE, DE/**/LETE, pg_shadow, safe parameterized SELECT) + exported vendor-tools.json schema.

All container artifacts live under tests/e2e_containers/ (keeping core verity-redteam-core runtime strictly zero-Docker per AGENTS.md).

docs.text:
tests/e2e_containers/verify_all_scenarios.sh executes and validates all 6 customer scenarios, exporting sanitized verbatim outputs into tests/e2e_containers/snapshots/:

  1. Scenario 1 — Workstation Config, Secret Scrubbing, Shell Wrapper & OSV CVE Audit:
  2. Commands:
    • verity scan (auto-discovers generated ~/.cursor/mcp.json, ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json, ~/.continue/config.yaml, ./.mcp.json)

    • verity scan --format json --output /tmp/out/scan.json
    • verity scan --format markdown --output /tmp/out/scan.md

  3. Assertions:

    • --fail-on-findings exits 1.
    • Reports SEC-STATIC-SECRET-IN-CONFIG, SEC-STATIC-UNSAFE-SHELL-WRAPPER, YAML Continue config findings, and OSV CVE match (CVE-2025-6514 for mcp-remote@0.1.15 when dataset/cache is present or pre-warmed cleanly).
    • Zero raw secret values appear anywhere in stdout, scan.json, scan.md, or scan.html (must show ****).

  4. Scenario 2 — Live Vulnerable MCP Server Probing (stdio & HTTP/SSE) + Schema Screen:

  5. Commands:

  6. Assertions:

    • Also probe a clean/benign fixture MCP server and assert exit 0.

  7. Scenario 3 — Deterministic SQL AST Guard (CLI + Python Library Import):

  8. Commands:

    • verity test --sql "SELECT id FROM users; DROP TABLE users;--" -> assert FAIL, exit 1
    • verity test --sql "DE/**/LETE FROM users" -> assert FAIL, exit 1

  9. Scenario 4 — Python AST Source Code Scanner (CI/CD PR Gate):

  10. Commands:

docs.title: M9: Dynamic, Narrow Terminal Screencast GIF (Charmbracelet VHS in Docker)
docs.text:
• Task ID: M9
  • Priority: P1
  • Status: Done
  • Dependencies: M7, M8
  • Blocks: M10
  • Target Repository: /Users/ivan/Project/3t.tools.intellij/verityredteam-free (verity-redteam-core)

docs.title: 1. Problem Statement & Audit Findings
docs.text:
The current hero visual in README.md (docs/assets/demo.svg, 59,979 bytes, 1285 × 1975.6 px) has three major problems: 1. It is completely static: demo.svg is a single-frame Rich SVG export with zero CSS @keyframes, <animate>, or SMIL/GIF motion — it does not animate or transition across scenarios at all. 2. It is oversized vertically: At 1975.6 px tall, it creates a huge wall-of-text image on GitHub instead of a compact, scannable screencast. 3. It has a stale package command: Line 289 of docs/assets/demo.svg displays $ uvx --from verity-core verity scan, whereas pyproject.toml uses package name verity-redteam-core.

Customers evaluating a CLI security tool on GitHub want a crisp, narrow, genuinely dynamic terminal video/GIF showing real commands being typed and real security findings appearing live.

docs.title: 2. Confirmed Technical Specification
docs.text:
• Tooling: Charmbracelet VHS (docs/assets/demo.tape) executed reproducibly inside a clean Docker recording container (ghcr.io/charmbracelet/vhs or custom recording image with vhs, ttyd, ffmpeg, gifsicle, Python 3.12, freshly installed verity-redteam-core, and M8 demo fixtures).
  • Dimensions & Visual Constraints (Narrow & Above-the-Fold):
  • Set Width 860 (hard limit: <= 900 px)
  • Set Height 440 (hard limit: <= 480 px)
  • Set FontSize 14, Set Padding 16, Set WindowBar Colorful (~88–92 cols × ~22 rows so Rich tables never wrap awkwardly)
  • Set Framerate 18 (between 15 and 20), Set TypingSpeed 40ms, infinite loop (LoopOffset / default loop)
  • Post-optimization via gifsicle -O3 --lossy=30 --colors 128 targeting < 2.5 MB (< 1.5 MB preferred) for fast loading on GitHub README.
  • No Fake Hardcoded Output: Every frame must be recorded from live executions of verity against real/fixture vulnerable targets (from M8) inside the recording container.

docs.title: 3. Dynamic 4-Scene Storyboard (~24 Seconds Total)
docs.text:
Scene Time Command Typed Live What Appears Dynamically on Screen 1. Workstation Secret & Config Audit 0–6s verity scan --config-file ~/.cursor/mcp.json Live Rich summary & findings table showing plaintext secret caught and scrubbed (KEY=****), unsafe bash -c wrapper flagged, and poisoned schema detected (CRITICAL/HIGH). 2. Live Poisoned MCP Probe 6–12s verity test --command "python vuln_mcp.py" Clear transition, live stdio probe output streaming FAIL rows for Prompt Injection Override (CWE-74), Tool Poisoning (CWE-358), and Exfil Webhook (CWE-200). 3. Deterministic SQL AST Guard 12–18s verity test --sql "SELECT id FROM users; DROP TABLE users;--" followed by verity test --sql "SELECT id, email FROM orders WHERE tenant_id = :tenant_id" Immediate red FAIL blocking stacked SQL injection (TokenType.SEMICOLON), followed by green PASS on safe parameterized SELECT. 4. 4-Target Demo & Python AST Gate 18–24s verity test --demo and verity scan --path ./vuln_mcp.py --fail-on-findings Shows 4/4 PASS zero-Docker checks (SQLite, Postgres, Mongo, Code Exec) and AST scan flagging eval() (CWE-94) + shell=True (CWE-78) with exit 1.

(Note: Keep prompt concise e.g. $ instead of long container paths, and Clear between scenes so every scene fits cleanly inside 860 × 440 without clipped tables.)

  2. scripts/record_demo_gif.sh (plus small recording Dockerfile if needed under tests/e2e_containers/ or scripts/) — One-command reproducible container recorder that installs verity-redteam-core wheel + M8 fixtures, runs vhs docs/assets/demo.tape, optimizes with gifsicle, and validates GIF properties.

docs.title: 1. Research Findings: verityredteam-free Current State
docs.text:
Our sub-agent inspected verityredteam-free (README.md, TASK_BOARD.md, docs/, src/verity/, and tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py):

  1. Repository & Visibility:
  2. Public GitHub repository (https://github.com/JMartynov/verityredteam-free), meaning GitHub Pages is 100% free and publicly accessible as soon as .github/workflows/pages.yml is pushed.
  3. Currently has 4 workflows (ci.yml, full-tests.yml, e2e-containers.yml, workflow.yaml for PyPI) and no GitHub Pages deployment workflow.
  4. Existing Documentation Assets:
  5. README.md (~40 KB): Massive single-file monolith containing hero badges, CLI reference, SAST/AST rule tables, SQL Guard dialects, MCP server setup, and architecture diagrams.
  6. TASK_BOARD.md: Milestone registry linked to GitHub Project Board #5 (PVTI_... item IDs).
  7. docs/extensibility.md, docs/releases/v0.2.0.md, docs/assets/demo.gif, and task specs in docs/tasks/.
  8. Existing Automated Documentation Parity Guard (tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py):
  9. verityredteam-free already has a 177-test deterministic parity suite that verifies README.md, TASK_BOARD.md, docs/tasks/M*.md, static rule IDs (VERITY-STATIC-*), AST rule IDs (VERITY-AST-*), and demo CWEs (CWE-89, CWE-639, CWE-943, CWE-94).
  10. Our web documentation portal and per-task publisher can hook directly into test_documentation_parity.py so no task can pass uv run pytest unless its web documentation page and task changelog entry are published and valid.

docs.title: 2. Technology Stack Comparison (Evaluated with DeepSeek)
docs.text:
Criterion Option A: MkDocs Material (Recommended) Option B: VitePress Option C: Astro Starlight Toolchain in verityredteam-free 100% Python (uv run --group docs mkdocs build) — zero package.json or Node.js needed Requires Node.js + npm/pnpm alongside uv Requires Node.js + npm/pnpm alongside uv Design & Aesthetics Modern Dark/Light Slate & Cyber-Indigo theme, sticky top navigation tabs, instant SPA navigation, code copy/annotations, terminal animations (demo.gif) Minimal Vue/Vite docs theme High-contrast Astro docs theme Search Experience Instant client-side search (/ or ⌘K) with fuzzy matching, rule ID lookup (VERITY-AST-CWE-94-EVAL), CLI flag search, and task tag filtering Client-side MiniSearch (⌘K) Pagefind static WASM search (⌘K) Automated Task-to-Docs Integration Pure Python script (scripts/build_docs_portal.py) runs in pytest (test_documentation_parity.py) and MkDocs build hooks Requires separate Python-to-Node build bridge Requires separate Python-to-Astro content sync Mermaid, Alerts & Math Native support for mermaid diagrams, GitHub alerts (> [!NOTE], > [!IMPORTANT]), and code tabs Needs community Markdown plugins Needs Astro integrations

[!TIP] Why MkDocs Material is the Ideal Fit for verityredteam-free: Keeping verityredteam-free 100% Python (uv) means contributors and sub-agents can preview (uv run mkdocs serve), build (uv run mkdocs build --strict), and verify (uv run pytest tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py) the entire web documentation portal in < 2 seconds without installing Node.js.

docs.title: 4. How Every Task Automatically Publishes to the Web Documentation
docs.text:
Every task in verityredteam-free (M7..M38+ in docs/tasks/M*.md and TASK_BOARD.md) will automatically publish to the documentation site through a 3-part deterministic pipeline:

sequenceDiagram
    participant Agent as Sub-Agent + DeepSeek (aider_bridge.py)
    participant Script as scripts/build_docs_portal.py
    participant Parity as tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py
    participant Actions as GitHub Actions (.github/workflows/pages.yml)
    participant Pages as GitHub Pages (jmartynov.github.io/verityredteam-free/)

    Agent->>Agent: 1. Implement task code + update target user guide in `docs/`
    Agent->>Script: 2. Run `uv run python scripts/build_docs_portal.py`
    Note over Script: Parses `TASK_BOARD.md`, `docs/tasks/M*.md`, and `src/verity/` rules/CLI<br/>Generates `docs/roadmap/index.md`, `docs/changelog/tasks.md`,<br/>and `docs/rules/catalog.md`
    Agent->>Parity: 3. Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py`
    Note over Parity: Fails if task has no `doc_targets`, if generated docs are stale,<br/>or if `mkdocs build --strict` has any broken link
    Agent->>Actions: 4. Merge worktree & push to `main`
    Actions->>Pages: 5. Builds MkDocs Material & deploys live in <30s

docs.title: What Gets Published Automatically When a Task Completes:
docs.text:
1. Feature Documentation Update (doc_targets Contract):
  2. Every task file in docs/tasks/M<NN>_<slug>.md specifies a doc_targets: list in its frontmatter/header pointing to the user-facing guide page(s) it updates (e.g., M30 updates docs/getting-started/installation.md; M33 updates docs/rules/typescript-sast.md).
  3. Auto-Generated Milestone & Task Dashboard (docs/roadmap/index.md):
  4. scripts/build_docs_portal.py reads TASK_BOARD.md and docs/tasks/M*.md to render a visual progress dashboard with status pills (Done, Ready, In Progress), GitHub Project Board #5 links (PVTI_...), and 1-click links to each task's specification and ATDD matrix.
  5. Auto-Generated Task Release Feed (docs/changelog/tasks.md):
  6. Whenever a task transitions to Done, scripts/build_docs_portal.py publishes a structured release card to the Task Release Feed showing the task summary, the acceptance criteria (AC-NN.1..AC-NN.K) verified, and clickable links to the updated documentation pages.
  7. Auto-Generated Live Rule & CLI Catalog (docs/rules/catalog.md):
  8. Introspects src/verity/screening/ and src/verity/guards/ at build time so every new SAST/AST rule or SQL dialect added by future tasks (M33–M37) appears automatically in the searchable Rule Catalog table.
  9. Enforced by test_documentation_parity.py:
  10. We extend tests/unit/test_documentation_parity.py so any task marked Done in TASK_BOARD.md / docs/tasks/M*.md is verified to have:
    • Valid doc_targets pointing to existing .md pages in docs/.
    • An up-to-date entry in the generated portal index (scripts/build_docs_portal.py --check).
    • Zero broken internal links in mkdocs.yml navigation.

docs.text:
Once you approve this proposal, we will execute it incrementally in verityredteam-free:
